title: Links, Images, and Paths
description: Connect pages and embed media: master hyperlink anchors (), image embeddings (), relative versus absolute path resolution, and accessible alt text design.

objectives.statement: Construct hyperlink anchor elements targeting internal relative routes and external URLs.
Embed images with src paths and meaningful, accessible alt text descriptions.

content.title: Weaving the Web with Links and Media
content.hook: The web is not an island of isolated pages — it is an interconnected mesh of hyperlinks and embedded media assets.
content.context: Anchors (``) turn text and images into clickable links, while `` pulls media into your layout. Getting file paths right (`./` for current folder, `../` for parent folder) is essential to prevent broken links and missing images.
goals: Create functional navigation links with `<a href="...">`.
Embed images with correct `src` paths and accessible `alt` descriptions.
Resolve relative paths across nested directory structures.

content.title: Directory Tree and Path Resolution
content.description: Root / (index.html, /blog/post.html, /images/logo.png). From `index.html`: `src="images/logo.png"` or `href="blog/post.html"`. From `blog/post.html`: `src="../images/logo.png"` (step up one directory) or `href="../index.html"`.

content.prompt: You are editing the file `/pages/tutorials/intro.html`. You want to display an image located at `/assets/images/diagram.png`. Which relative path correctly locates the image?

feedback.correct: Spot on! From `/pages/tutorials/`, `../` moves up to `/pages/`, and another `../` moves up to the root `/`, allowing you to traverse into `assets/images/diagram.png`.
feedback.incorrect: Count the directory levels: `intro.html` is 2 levels deep inside `/pages/tutorials/`. You must ascend two directories with `../../` to reach `/assets/`.

content.title: Build a Linked Profile Card
content.prompt: Create a profile card containing an accessible `` (with `src="https://placehold.co/100"` and a descriptive `alt="Jane Doe profile photo"`) and a navigation link (`View Portfolio`).
content.starterCode:
Jane Doe

Frontend Engineer & UI Architect.

testCases.description: Profile card must contain an with src and alt attributes
testCases.assertion: document.querySelector('.profile-card img') && document.querySelector('.profile-card img').getAttribute('src') && document.querySelector('.profile-card img').getAttribute('alt')

testCases.description: Profile card must contain an <a> link targeting /portfolio.html
testCases.assertion: document.querySelector('.profile-card a') && document.querySelector('.profile-card a').getAttribute('href') === '/portfolio.html' && document.querySelector('.profile-card a').textContent.includes('View Portfolio')

feedback.correct: Great work! You authored a fully accessible profile card with proper image attributes and hyperlinked navigation.
feedback.incorrect: Ensure your `` has both `src` and non-empty `alt` attributes, and your `` has `href="/portfolio.html"` with text 'View Portfolio'.

content.prompt: When should an image have a descriptive `alt` text versus an empty `alt=""` attribute? What happens if you omit the `alt` attribute entirely?

feedback.correct: Excellent! Informative images require descriptive alt text; purely decorative images need `alt=""` so screen readers ignore them. Omitting `alt` entirely causes screen readers to read the raw file URL!
feedback.incorrect: Explain the difference between informative images (descriptive alt), decorative images (empty alt), and missing alt attributes.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Links and Media
takeaways: Use `<a href="...">` to create accessible hyperlinks.
Use `` with void tag syntax; never omit the `alt` attribute.
Relative paths use `./` (current directory) and `../` (parent directory) to traverse folder trees.
Always provide descriptive alt text for meaningful images and empty `alt=""` for decorative graphics.
